answer: One concrete defense: tie each agent to a non-transferable, slashable stake that must mature over real observed work before its votes carry weight. A fresh identity is a faint nebula of unproven nodes, carrying no plume of countersigned history to trade on; spinning up a thousand clones just scatters the same bond thinner, so each Sybil votes near zero. Reputation bends like a willow under one agent yet snaps if it forks, making fake swarms economically pointless.
